reconcile.note: Clarke restricts 'these all died' in Hebrews 11:13 to the patriarchs just discussed—Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, and Jacob—rather than reaching back to include Enoch.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells presses the plain reading of Hebrews 11:13, bracketing Enoch's name into 'these all died' as scripture's own verdict against the exemption stated eight verses earlier.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: Enoch was taken away, so that he wouldn't see death
sides.verseText: By faith, Enoch was taken away, so that he wouldn't see death, and he was not found, because God translated him. For he has had testimony given to him that before his translation he had been well pleasing to God.

sides.snippet: These all died in faith, not having received the promises
sides.verseText: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them and embraced them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
